title: Mighty Five Long Weekend
subtitle: Finish Utah’s five national parks over a May–October three-day weekend: Timpanogos Cave and Arches on Day 1, Canyonlands and Capitol Reef on Day 2, home from Salt Lake City on Day 3.

days.title: Fly to Salt Lake
days.html:
✈︎

OAK → SLC after work

Clocks jump an hour forward. Pick up the round-trip rental at SLC, ideally AWD (Costco Travel). AWD matters most in winter, for the mountain passes in and out.

Sleep at the Best Western Plus Airport Inn & Suites, 5433 W Wiley Post Way.

Navigate to hotel ↗
Winter: check UDOT road conditions before bed for the drive over Soldier Summit.
Once dates are set: book OAK ⇄ SLC flights, the three hotels and the AWD rental, and check whether Arches needs timed entry on your dates. Home flight any time after about 3:30 PM Mountain on Day 3.

days.title: Timpanogos Cave, then Arches
days.sub: Salt Lake City → Timpanogos Cave → Arches → Moab
days.cut: Timpanogos Cave’s visitor center is seasonal (about mid-May to mid-October). Outside the season, skip it and leave SLC at 8:00. Arches roads and viewpoints can ice over after snow.

days.title: Island in the Sky, then Capitol Reef
days.cut: No gas inside Canyonlands, so fill the tank in Moab. Capitol Reef’s visitor center may close on major holidays, so keep this a non-holiday day.

days.title: A slow morning, then home
days.sub: Capitol Reef Scenic Drive → Salt Lake City
days.cut: No gas between Salina and Loa, so fill up in Torrey. In winter, check UDOT for the high road between Loa and I-70.

stops.via: I-15 S → Exit 284 (Alpine–Highland) → SR-92 east 10 mi up American Fork Canyon. Put “Timpanogos Cave National Monument” into GPS, not a street address.
stops.name: Timpanogos Cave NM
stops.place: Timpanogos Cave Visitor Center, American Fork Canyon
stops.hrs: Seasonal: usually open with the cave tour season, about mid-May to mid-October, 7:00–5:30. Closed in winter. (801) 756-5239.
stops.optional: Outside the season, skip this stop and leave SLC at 8:00 for Arches.
stops.acc: Stamp only. The visitor center is at the bottom of the cave trail, by the parking. The cave itself is a steep 1.5-mile hike up, so skip it.
stops.about: Three small caves high on Mount Timpanogos, joined by man-made tunnels and protected since 1922. They’re known for helictites, twisting formations that seem to defy gravity.

stops.via: Back to I-15 S → US-6 over Soldier Summit → I-70 → US-191. Drive time is an estimate; confirm in Google Maps.
stops.name: Arches NP
stops.hrs: Winter 9:00–4:30 daily, longer the rest of the year; closed only on Christmas.
stops.warn: Timed-entry reservations weren’t required in 2026, but have applied in busy months before. Check once dates are set.
stops.about: More than 2,000 natural stone arches, the densest concentration anywhere, carved from red Entrada sandstone.

stops.name: Arches Scenic Drive
stops.addr: The Windows Section, Arches National Park
stops.note: Park Avenue viewpoint, Balanced Rock right beside the road, then the Windows section, where the arches are visible from the parking area. Finish at the Delicate Arch lower viewpoint, a short walk from its lot.
stops.warn: Roads and viewpoints can ice over or close after snow.

stops.name: Moab, UT
stops.addr: Best Western Plus Canyonlands Inn, 16 S Main St, Moab, UT
stops.note: Best Western Plus Canyonlands Inn, 16 S Main St. Downtown on Main Street, with dinner within walking distance. Tomorrow starts at 8:20 AM.

stops.via: US-191 N → Scenic Byway 313, 32 mi. Fill the tank first.
stops.name: Canyonlands NP
stops.place: Island in the Sky Visitor Center
stops.addr: Island in the Sky Visitor Center
stops.where: Island in the Sky Visitor Center
stops.hrs: Winter 9:00–4:00, longer the rest of the year; closed only on Christmas.
stops.ok: New park for the 64. The Shafer Canyon overlook is next to the visitor center. Then drive on to Grand View Point at the end of the road, a short walk from the car. The Needles district closes in winter, so Island in the Sky is the reliable stop.
stops.about: The Colorado and Green rivers split Canyonlands into districts. Island in the Sky is a mesa standing more than 1,000 feet above the canyons below.

stops.via: Back to US-191 → I-70 → UT-24 via Hanksville.
stops.name: Capitol Reef NP
stops.hrs: Open daily, with shorter hours in winter. Call 435-425-3791 the week before to confirm.
stops.ok: New park for the 64, and Utah is done. The Fremont petroglyph panel is along UT-24 just east of the visitor center, with a short boardwalk from its parking area.
stops.about: Protects the Waterpocket Fold, a nearly 100-mile wrinkle in the Earth’s crust. The Fruita orchards were planted by Mormon pioneers.

stops.name: Torrey, UT
stops.note: Capitol Reef Resort. It was long listed as a Best Western, so confirm the brand when booking. The sandstone cliffs behind Torrey glow red at sunset.

stops.name: Capitol Reef Scenic Drive
stops.note: The paved first stretch runs past the Fruita orchards and under the Waterpocket Fold cliffs. Turn back when it suits you.
stops.ok: The Gifford House and its pies are open mid-March to late November only.

stops.via: UT-24 → UT-72 → I-70 → US-50 → I-15 N. No gas between Salina and Loa, so fill up in Torrey.
stops.title: Salt Lake City → home
stops.note: Lunch in Salt Lake, return the car, and fly home any time after about 3:30 PM Mountain. You land back on Pacific time, an hour earlier by the clock.
